ledger.note: 1805: Napoleon creates the Principality of Lucca and Piombino for his sister Elisa and Felice Baciocchi. The page: 'was created in July 1805' (the infobox lists the Treaty of Pressburg, 23 June 1805; the constitution is dated 22 June 1805); Piombino 'bestowed by Napoleon upon his sister Elisa' in March 1805. Lucca and Piombino were 'ruled as a single monarchy'.

ledger.note: 1814: Austrian troops occupy Lucca. With Napoleon's fall the 'Imperial Austrian Army occupied Lucca, ending French control'. The page does not date the day and says nothing of Piombino, Massa or the Garfagnana in 1814. Confidence lowered from 3 to 2: the page names only Lucca ('the Imperial Austrian Army occupied Lucca'), not Piombino, Massa-Carrara or the Garfagnana. [Reviewer eu-20-x, 2026-11-01]

1815: Piombino goes to Tuscany. The Congress 'bestowed the duchy' of Lucca on Maria Louisa, and Piombino 'was given to the Grand Duchy of Tuscany' (the page dates the settlement 1814-1815; the Duchy of Lucca page gives the Congress of Vienna date 9 June 1815).

notes: New dossier, a state Cliopatria lacks (the republic-of-lucca dossier names it as successor, and grand-duchy-of-tuscany records Piombino as a gain from it in 1815). Pages are thin: no area, no infobox dissolution date, no 1814 day. The state's identity after 1809 is ambiguous: the page says Lucca and Piombino 'became part of' the Grand Duchy of Tuscany that Elisa ruled from 1809; the dossier keeps the principality alive to 1815 because the Congress of Vienna disposed of it. The merge counterpart 'Grand Duchy of Tuscany (Napoleonic)' is a name, not a dossier (it is not Cliopatria's grand-duchy-of-tuscany of the Habsburg-Lorraine line). Needs: a dossier or counterpart for the Duchy of Massa and Carrara (1806 annexation) and for the Napoleonic Tuscany. Names the gazetteer lacks: Piombino (place), Garfagnana (region).
